## Comparability caveat

Four of the five carriers are clean calendar-year comparisons [DOC-1], but **Alaska Air Group's FY2024 is not a like-for-like full-year figure**. Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results are consolidated only from that date forward, contributing $869 million of revenue (and a $113 million net loss) to the period [DOC-2]. Alaska's FY2024 ratios therefore blend ~8.5 months of standalone Alaska with ~3.5 months of the combined entity, and the denominators/numerators are not on a consistent basis with the prior year or with the other four carriers' full-year operations. Alaska's rankings below should be treated as approximate.

## Fuel expense as % of revenue, FY2024 (lowest first)

| Rank | Airline | Fuel / Revenue | Source figures |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | **17.1%** | $10,566M / $61,643M [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | **20.6%** | $11,756M / $57,063M [DOC-1] |
| 3 | American | **21.1%** | $11,418M / $54,211M [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Southwest | **21.1%** | $5,812M / $27,483M [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Alaska | **21.4%** | $2,506M / $11,735M [DOC-1] |

American (21.06%) and Southwest (21.15%) are effectively tied — the gap is under 0.1 pp and is not meaningful.

## Salaries, wages and benefits as % of revenue, FY2024 (lowest first)

| Rank | Airline | Labor / Revenue | Source figures |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Delta | **26.2%** | $16,161M / $61,643M [DOC-1] |
| 2 | United | **29.2%** | $16,678M / $57,063M [DOC-1] |
| 3 | American | **29.6%** | $16,021M / $54,211M [DOC-1] |
| 4 | Alaska | **30.6%** | $3,588M / $11,735M [DOC-1] |
| 5 | Southwest | **44.5%** | $12,240M / $27,483M [DOC-1] |

## Answer to the comparison

Yes — **Delta ranks lowest (top-ranked) on both metrics**, at 17.1% fuel-to-revenue and 26.2% labor-to-revenue, consistent with its position as the largest revenue base ($61,643M) and highest operating income ($5,995M) of the group [DOC-1]. The orderings diverge only at the bottom: Southwest is middle-of-the-pack on fuel intensity but a clear outlier on labor intensity (44.5%, ~15 pp above the next-highest), which aligns with its thin $321M operating income [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Fuel % of revenue (lowest first): Delta 17.1%, United 20.6%, American 21.1%, Southwest 21.1%, Alaska 21.4%. Salaries/wages/benefits % of revenue (lowest first): Delta 26.2%, United 29.2%, American 29.6%, Alaska 30.6%, Southwest 44.5%. Yes — Delta is top-ranked (lowest) in both. Caveat: Alaska's FY2024 includes Hawaiian only from Sept 18, 2024, so its ratios are not fully comparable.
